titleText.es: Estoy enseñándole a decir esto a todo familiar de 8 años que tengo, y a todos los de 14 años a decir lo mismo de Toy Story. Además, Pokemom llegó a EEUU hace más de una década y los niños que nacieron después de que saliera Aladdin cumplirán 18 el año que viene.
titleText.en: I'm teaching every 8-year-old relative to say this, and every 14-year-old to do the same thing with Toy Story.  Also, Pokemon hit the US over a decade ago and kids born after Aladdin came out will turn 18 next year.
titleText.noteEn: The English title text is copied exactly from official xkcd, including its two-space sentence break. The Spanish archive has the genuine spelling Pokemom and otherwise adapts the same generation-gap examples. In the raster, 11S is the Spanish alphanumeric shorthand for the September 11 attacks and ROB is an unchanged proper name, so both are explicitly inventoried but not made vocabulary cards.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Encontraron is the completed-past form of encontrar for they or formal plural you. The stem stays encontr- and the -aron ending marks an -ar verb's completed plural action.
Fantasma ends in -a but is normally masculine when it names a ghost: el fantasma.
Chorra is an informal Spain description for something foolish, trivial, or unimpressive. It is the feminine singular form, used with a feminine naming word such as historia.

example.en: It was a really lame excuse.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tío literally means an uncle. Before a relative's name in direct address, it functions like the English family title “Uncle.” This is distinct from the informal Spain use meaning “guy.”

cardDefinitions.answerEn: gives; causes (special form for a sought scary thing)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dé is a form of dar. The accent distinguishes it from the preposition de. Here the speaker asks about an unspecified story that might cause more fear, so dar appears in this special subjunctive form.

example.es: Busco una película que dé miedo.
example.en: I am looking for a movie that is scary.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Intenta is the affirmative command for one familiar person, and lo stands for the thing to try. Lo attaches to the command, and the written accent keeps the original stress: inténtalo.
Sucedió is the completed-past form of suceder for one event or thing.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: was born (special form after antes de que)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Naciera is a past-looking subjunctive form of nacer. Antes de que uses this form because the birth is viewed as the later event relative to what happened before it.

example.es: La casa existía antes de que yo naciera.
example.en: The house existed before I was born.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I am (stating age); literally, I have
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish uses tener, “to have,” when stating age. Tengo is the form for the speaker: tengo edad suficiente means “I am old enough.”

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; enough for the following action
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After suficiente, para introduces the action that the amount, ability, or age is enough to perform. The following action stays in its unchanged dictionary form.

example.en: There is enough light to read.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to carry on; to have (a conversation)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mantener often means “to keep” or “to maintain.” With conversación, it describes having or carrying on the exchange.

example.es: Es fácil mantener una conversación con ella.
example.en: It is easy to carry on a conversation with her.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone is old enough to do something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of tener, then edad suficiente para and the action in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tener changes for the person: tengo, tienes, tiene, and so on. Edad suficiente para stays together, and the following -ar, -er, or -ir verb does not change.

example.es: Ya tiene edad suficiente para viajar solo.
example.en: He is old enough to travel alone now.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: 11S · antes de nacer · edad suficiente para conversar
cardDefinitions.answerEn: the frightening realization that someone born after the September 11 attacks is already old enough to hold a conversation
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The September 11 attacks occurred in 2001, while this comic appeared in 2009. The child's line compresses that growing time gap into an ordinary conversation and makes the older relative feel the passage of time more sharply than the ghost story did. The title text extends the same joke to younger relatives and older popular culture.

applications.explanationEn: Una leaves the feminine thing unidentified, and que introduces dé in the special form used for the sought scarier example.
Dé supplies the matching form of dar for the unspecified story, while miedo names the fear it would cause.
Intenta is the affirmative informal singular command of intentar.
Lo attaches to the affirmative command intenta, and the written accent preserves the original stress.

applications.explanationEn: Antes de que places the speaker's birth after the earlier event, and naciera uses the special past-looking subjunctive form for that later event.
Sin embargo marks the age statement as a contrast with having been born after the earlier event.
Tengo matches the speaker, edad suficiente para expresses being old enough, and mantener stays in its unchanged dictionary form for the resulting action.
Mantener combines with conversación to describe carrying on the exchange; esta identifies which conversation without changing the expression's core words.
